claim: The Carlsbad Flower Fields are open seasonally (roughly March through mid-May), 9am-6pm daily at 5704 Paseo del Norte, with peak ranunculus bloom late March through April; tickets must be bought online in advance.
quote: Peak ranunculus bloom occurs in late March through April... Hours: 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. daily (Entrance gate closes at 5:30 p.m.)... All tickets must be purchased before arrival

claim: The Carlsbad Flower Fields run March through May only, with ranunculus peaking late March through April, about 30 miles / 30 minutes north of downtown San Diego.
quote: The Flower Fields operate March-May exclusively. The peak blooming of the ranunculus is in late March through April.

claim: From San Diego, Temecula wine country is about 60 miles (under an hour), and Julian is roughly 90 minutes away at 4,225 feet elevation, known for apples and apple pie with fall apple season Sep-Nov.
quote: Julian is a small town in the mountains about 90 minutes from San Diego, famous for exactly one thing: apples and apple pie. The town sits at 4,225 feet elevation

claim: Temecula Valley has over 40 wineries spread along three wine trails (Rancho California Road, Calle Contento, De Portola Road), about 45-60 minutes north of San Diego, with Old Town tastings typically 4-6 wines for $10-20.
quote: Temecula Valley boasts dozens of wineries along three wine trails - Rancho California Road, Calle Contento and De Portola Road... Most tastings in Old Town Temecula include 4-6 wines for $10-20 per person

claim: MTS Route 992 stops at both airport terminals and reaches downtown's Santa Fe Depot in about 15 minutes for a $2.50 one-way fare, running every 15 minutes seven days a week, connecting to three Trolley lines, Rapid buses, COASTER and Amtrak.
quote: Route 992 stops on the elevated platform at both terminals and takes only 15 minutes to get to/from Santa Fe Depot... every 15 minutes for most of the day, 7 days a week. One-way fares are just $2.50

claim: The San Diego Flyer is a free electric shuttle connecting the airport to the Old Town Transit Center seven days a week, where travelers transfer to the Trolley, MTS buses, COASTER and Amtrak.
quote: The San Diego Flyer is a free electric shuttle-bus service that connects the airport to regional transit and operates seven days a week between the airport and the Old Town Transit Center

claim: Downtown San Diego is highly walkable, with the Gaslamp Quarter offering lodging, dining, shopping and entertainment within a single square mile, letting many visitors get around without a car.
quote: Downtown San Diego is an incredibly walkable area, and many visitors are able to enjoy the city without ever getting in a car!

claim: September and October are the best months to visit San Diego (warm 70s, swimmable ocean, thinner crowds, lower rates); May/June bring May Gray and June Gloom marine-layer overcast, and July-August are peak crowds with Comic-Con week selling out downtown hotels.
quote: May Gray and June Gloom bring overcast coastal skies from mid-May through June, though clouds typically clear by afternoon... July and August peak with crowds and premium pricing

claim: The best times to visit San Diego are March-May and September-November, with overcast May Gray and June Gloom days common as a marine layer blankets the coast and usually burns off by early afternoon.
quote: During May and June, overcast days occur often, so much so that locals designate the months as May Gray and June Gloom... The clouds usually burn off by early afternoon

claim: A car-free Tijuana day trip is easy via the MTS Blue Line Trolley from downtown's Santa Fe Depot to the San Ysidro border (about 40-50 minutes, ~17 miles), a short walk to the PedEast/PedWest pedestrian crossings.
quote: the easiest way to cross to Tijuana from San Diego is usually via the San Diego trolley, starting at downtown's Santa Fe Depot and hopping on the Blue Line straight to the San Ysidro border station. The trolley trip from downtown San Diego to the border takes about 40-50 minutes.

claim: As of 2025 the PedWest (El Chaparral) pedestrian crossing runs limited hours and is closed for entry into Mexico, so day-trippers should use the main PedEast crossing at the San Ysidro Port of Entry near the trolley station.
quote: As of September 2025, PedWest is open for limited hours in each direction during the day... PedWest is closed going into Mexico and only open from 6:00 to 14:00 each day going back to the U.S.

claim: A sensible first-timer 3-day San Diego itinerary devotes one day to Balboa Park/Zoo, one to La Jolla and the coast, and one to Coronado plus the harbor or Old Town, basing downtown or Little Italy; a car adds flexibility between neighborhoods.
quote: one day around Balboa Park, one day around La Jolla and the coast, and one final day around Coronado, the harbor, or Old Town... For a first trip, the easiest base is usually Downtown, Little Italy, or near the harbor.
